# Sebastian Esteva

> Also known as Sebastian Kellc Esteva. Stanford-trained engineer and communicator who builds at the intersection of human experience, technology, and design — and chooses his work by what he believes will make the world better.

Sebastian Esteva holds a B.S. in Biomechanical Engineering from Stanford (2026) and is completing an M.A. in Communication — Media Studies (anticipated 2027). He works across product design, wearable technology, VR/AR research, and strategic communications — always following work he finds genuinely inspiring. He is a Research Assistant at Stanford's Virtual Human Interaction Lab (VHIL), studying how virtual and augmented reality shape human behavior and decision-making. His capstone research examines how specific technology variables — degrees of freedom, fidelity, and related hardware/software features — affect sense of presence in virtual worlds.

He is also a Maker on Duty at Maker Nexus (Stanford's fabrication space), a Teaching Assistant for Stanford's Neurobiology of Pain course, and a founding Resident Leader of Explore Energy, Stanford's energy-focused residential community.

Sebastian brings the same intensity to his civic work. He has advocated for gun-violence prevention at national conferences in New York City and Washington, D.C. — rooms that included President Biden and NYC Mayor Eric Adams — as a Community Engagement Intern at Everytown for Gun Safety. He is strongly principled, hard-working, and drawn to problems that matter.

Beyond his technical and professional work, Sebastian has 18 years of Aikido practice (Black Belt), a deep love of film — both watching and making it, and is a fluent Spanish speaker born in Mexico and raised in the United States. He is motivated by the intersection of human experience and the creation of wonder through design — asking not just "does it work?" but "what does it say?"

This portfolio was built from scratch and deployed via GitHub. It reflects his aesthetic sensibility: minimal, dark, typographically deliberate.

## Pages

- [Home](https://sesteva.com/): Portfolio landing page with featured projects, work experience highlights, and contact. Dark, Apple-inspired aesthetic with scroll-triggered animations.
- [Where I've Worked](https://sesteva.com/experience.html): Full work history spanning Stanford research labs, startups, nonprofits, and community organizations — including VHIL, Guidewheel, ExploreTech, and Everytown for Gun Safety.
- [Poser Chess Set](https://sesteva.com/chess.html): A hand-crafted chess set built as a physical fabrication project, exploring form, material, and process.
- [Graduation Pendant](https://sesteva.com/pendant.html): A custom silver pendant cast in the shape of "26" — his graduation year. Intentionally light-themed and image-led; the piece speaks for itself.
- [The Slip Door](https://sesteva.com/slipdoor.html): A fully operational, full-scale prototype of an accessible automatic sliding car door, built for Volkswagen's Future of Entry challenge. Increased entrance volume by 253% for mobility-impaired drivers. Built with a team of four Stanford engineers.
- [Bastón](https://sesteva.com/baston.html): A hand-built, foldable wooden cane designed and machined for his grandmother — combining lathe-turned wood with a precision metal folding mechanism. A personal project at the intersection of engineering and care.
- [Time Collector](https://sesteva.com/timecollector.html): A 24-inch kinetic marble clock sculpture built with a team of four, combining laser-cut wood and 3D-printed gears into a fully functional timekeeping mechanism.
- [HP's Reckoning with Company Values](https://sesteva.com/hp-reckoning-corporate-espionage.html): Strategy case study on HP's 2006 spying scandal — crisis communications, corporate governance, and values-based leadership.
- [Shape Optimization & Generative Design](https://sesteva.com/algorithmic-modeling-shape-optimization.html): ME 127 engineering project applying FEA-driven shape optimization and generative design to redesign a machining gripper across materials and manufacturing methods.
- [Social Engineering via Predictive Algorithms](https://sesteva.com/social-engineering-predictive-algorithms.html): Academic paper examining how predictive algorithms enable political micro-targeting and reshape democratic citizenship.
